name: SF to LA Road Trip
summary: A 3-day coastal road trip from San Francisco to Los Angeles via Highway 1. Expect stunning cliff views, fresh seafood, and at least one stop that makes you consider moving there.

stops.name: San Francisco
stops.goal: Start the trip — fuel up and hit the coast

stops.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
stops.goal: See the sea otters and the kelp forest — one of the best aquariums in the world
stops.note: Book online to skip the line. The Open Sea exhibit is unmissable.

alts.name: Monterey State Beach
alts.goal: Skip the aquarium and walk the beach instead — free and just as memorable

alts.name: Cannery Row
alts.goal: Walk Cannery Row for shops and people-watching instead of the aquarium

stops.name: Big Sur River Inn
stops.goal: Overnight stay — creekside rooms in the heart of Big Sur
stops.note: Book a creekside room. Restaurant on site — the apple pie is famous.

stops.name: McWay Falls
stops.goal: Quick photo stop — waterfall dropping onto a secluded beach
stops.addr: Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park, CA-1, Big Sur, CA 93920
stops.note: Easy overlook trail, no hiking required. Morning light is best for photos.

stops.name: Hearst Castle
stops.goal: Tour the most absurd private home in American history
stops.addr: 750 Hearst Castle Rd, San Simeon, CA 93452
stops.note: Book the Grand Rooms tour in advance — it's the best first-timer option.

stops.name: Solvang
stops.goal: Stretch and grab a Danish pastry in a surreal Danish-themed town
stops.note: Try Olsen's Danish Village Bakery. The æbleskiver (pancake balls) are the move.

stops.name: Santa Barbara Inn
stops.goal: Overnight stay with ocean views in Santa Barbara
stops.addr: 901 E Cabrillo Blvd, Santa Barbara, CA 93103
stops.note: Ocean view rooms are worth the upgrade. Walk to the Funk Zone for wine tasting.

stops.name: Stearns Wharf
stops.goal: Walk the pier — fresh seafood and ocean views

stops.name: Santa Monica Pier
stops.goal: End of the road — touch the Route 66 sign, get the photo, call it done
stops.addr: 200 Santa Monica Pier, Santa Monica, CA 90401
stops.note: You made it. The pier is touristy but the symbolism is real. Sunset here is a solid finish.

stops.name: Hotel in Downtown LA
stops.goal: Final overnight — rest up before the real world resumes

routes.note: Take I-280 S to CA-1 S. Scenic but slower — budget extra time for photo pullouts.
CA-1 S. Bixby Bridge is a must-stop photo op — pullout on the north side.
Stop at McWay Falls on the way. Check Caltrans for CA-1 closures before this leg — washouts are common.
Elephant seal rookery at Piedras Blancas is worth a 10-min stop just north of Hearst Castle.
CA-154 for mountain views, or US-101 for speed. Take 154 if the weather is clear.
US-101 S to I-405 S. Traffic builds hard after 3pm — leave Santa Barbara by noon if you can.

days.note: SF to Big Sur — the best stretch of coastline in California

items.txt: Grab lunch on Cannery Row — the clam chowder in a sourdough bowl is not a cliché, it's just correct

days.note: Big Sur to Santa Barbara — castles, Danish towns, and ocean views

opts.txt: Walk State Street for shopping and wine tasting in the Funk Zone

days.note: Santa Barbara to LA — final stretch

opts.txt: Dinner in Venice Beach — try Gjelina on Abbot Kinney
Dinner in Santa Monica — try Cassia for Southeast Asian
Head to Koreatown for Korean BBQ — Park's BBQ if you want the best
